evidence: src/order/order.entity.ts: `@Entity('orders')` on class OrderEntity ties the class to a database table (persistence/infrastructure concern).
src/order/order.entity.ts: `@PrimaryGeneratedColumn('uuid') id` hands identity generation to the database/ORM (persistence concern).
src/order/order.entity.ts: `@Column()` decorators on customerId, quantity and total define the column mapping (persistence schema).
src/order/order.entity.ts: the class has no domain behaviour, invariants or business methods. It is only an ORM data model.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file sits in the domain layer because of the **/*.entity.ts pattern, but its only job is persistence mapping. OrderEntity is a TypeORM ORM model. It ties the class to the 'orders' table with @Entity('orders'). It sets up database key generation with @PrimaryGeneratedColumn('uuid') and maps each field to a column with @Column(). It has no domain behaviour, invariants or business rules. It is a database schema definition, which is infrastructure (persistence) work. The rubric names persistence logic in a domain file as a failure. Confidence is moderate, not high, because the layer model puts *.entity.ts files in domain on purpose, as is common in NestJS projects. Even so, the work the file actually does is persistence, not domain.

violations.message: OrderEntity carries persistence responsibilities that belong to the infrastructure layer, not the domain layer: it maps to the 'orders' table with @Entity('orders'), generates its key with @PrimaryGeneratedColumn('uuid') and maps columns with @Column() on customerId, quantity and total. It has no domain logic.
